title: Support Dock — runbook choreographer and operator station
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a unified 'Support Dock' operator surface that converts canonical runbooks into typed, execution-ready task bundles and provides a light-weight operator station for first-line responders. The dock will: (1) ingest runbook source (markdown + YAML metadata), (2) compile a task manifest with typed inputs/outputs and preflight checks, (3) attach telemetry/rollback hooks, and (4) expose a guarded execution surface with RBAC and dry-run simulation. This reduces time-to-remediate and ensures repeatability/cost-safety for common incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook ingestion pipeline accepts markdown runbooks with metadata and produces a task manifest (JSON) with typed params
Operator Station UI shows task inputs, estimated side-effects, and required RBAC in a single pane
Execution shim runs a dry-run and a guarded live-run with cancel/undo hooks
Telemetry emits structured events for each task step (start, step, retry, success, failure) to the ops-telemetry stream
Canary rollout: support team performs 50 supervised executions in a staging environment without incidents before GA
out_of_scope: Full runbook authoring experience (authoring lives in docs)
Replacing long-running automation engines — this is for short surgical flows (<= 10 steps)
engineering_notes: Task manifest bundler will reuse existing step-telemetry schema (ENG-712314) but extend with estimated side-effects and cost hints
Use existing RBAC library from admin-api and add an execution token shortlived scope
Runtime shim: small Node/Go service that runs step adapters in a sandboxed environment with timeout and audit logging
Prefer explicit prefight checks over optimistic runs: validate resources, quotas, and dependent services before live execution
security_checks: Audit log entries per task execution with actor and request id
Mandatory review banner for tasks that alter persistent customer data
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): runbook compiler + dry-run in staging (week 1)
Phase 1 (pilot): operator station + 2 small SRE teams, supervised live runs (week 2-3)
Phase 2 (canary): expand pilot to all oncall for low-risk playbooks (week 4)
Phase 3 (GA): open to support with training and docs (week 5)
Fallback: ability to disable Support Dock and revert to manual runbook steps if anomalies exceed threshold
metrics: MTTR reduction target: 20% for pilot playbooks
Run success rate target: >= 98% after pilot corrections
Mean dry-run time: < 2s for verification checks
Telem coverage: 100% of steps emit structured events
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overly trusted automation could escalate incidents. Mitigation: strict RBAC + explicit human confirmation for destructive steps
Risk: manifest mismatch with underlying infra. Mitigation: strong prefight validations and version pinning on adapters
Risk: noisy telemetry or alert storms. Mitigation: sampling and batching of non-critical events and alert thresholds for systemic failures
tasks: Schema extension for step metadata and side-effect hints
Build Operator Station UI mock and iterate with SRE team
Implement runtime shim with sandboxing and audit logging
Add telemetry hooks and dashboard in ops-console
Write operator playbook for pilot and training materials
